about: C16 S3-E synthetic development set. Written by the S3-E author for tuning only; it is NOT the retrieval oracle, its fixture or the blind holdout. Passages are fictional (no real case, person or holding is asserted). Topics were chosen to avoid the subject of the oracle's RET-07/RET-10 (prior notice of an allegation before a hearing), whose text the author had read in the C15 report; the phenomenon classes (no shared content word, paraphrase, contrary or conditional answer, answer buried in a long paragraph) are the ones C15 published as the failure mechanism. Real-sample passages (seeded, 3,000, seed 16) are added as distractors by the harness.

passages.title: Hav Rattan Lal v Union of India (synthetic)
passages.text: An injury suffered in a recreational game while away on furlough bears no causal connection with military duty; the claim to a disability award was rightly rejected and the application is dismissed.

passages.title: Sep Mohan Das v Union of India (synthetic)
passages.text: Condonation was refused. The applicant offered no explanation for remaining silent for over a decade, and stale grievances cannot be revived merely by sending a fresh representation to the authorities.

passages.title: Manual commentary on offences (synthetic)
passages.text: The distinguishing element is the intention never to come back; one who stays absent but always meant to rejoin commits only the lesser offence.

passages.title: Pension Regulations commentary (synthetic)
passages.text: The surviving spouse of a member killed in action is granted a liberalised family award at the enhanced rate, irrespective of length of engagement.

passages.title: Nk Joginder v Chief of Army Staff (synthetic)
passages.text: Termination by the competent authority on administrative grounds is valid where a court-martial is found inexpedient and the reasons are recorded in writing; both conditions were met and the petition fails.

passages.title: L/Nk Suresh v Union of India (synthetic)
passages.text: A statement extracted by a superior in the course of an informal inquiry cannot be relied upon at the subsequent proceedings unless it was voluntary and the maker was cautioned.

passages.title: Smt Kamla Devi v Controller of Defence Accounts (synthetic)
passages.text: Excess emoluments wrongly credited without any misrepresentation by the recipient may not be recouped from a retired or low-ranking member after a long lapse of time.

passages.title: Gnr Balbir Singh v Union of India (synthetic)
passages.text: The record shows that the convoy halted near the transit camp late in the evening and that the unit had been on the move for two days. Several witnesses described the quarrel over the allotment of tents, and the defence produced the duty roster to establish who was present. The trial court considered the medical evidence of the havildar's bruises and found the account of the scuffle consistent with it. Using criminal force against a superior in such circumstances is visited with dismissal and a term of imprisonment, and the sentence actually awarded was well within that limit. The remaining grounds concerned the composition of the court and the translation of a witness's statement, neither of which was raised at the trial.

passages.title: Ex-Sub Hari Prakash v Union of India (synthetic)
passages.text: Once he has ceased to be subject to the Act, proceedings may still be commenced only within six months of his release; the prosecution, initiated after nineteen months, was barred.

passages.title: Manual commentary on defences (synthetic)
passages.text: A command that is manifestly unlawful affords no defence to the subordinate who carries it out; obedience is owed only to lawful directions.

passages.title: Rfn Thapa v Union of India (synthetic)
passages.text: A disease not noted at the time of entry is presumed to have arisen during engagement; the burden lies on the employer to rebut that presumption with reasons.

passages.title: Rules commentary on proceedings (synthetic)
passages.text: A person tried is entitled, on request, to copies of the proceedings and of the evidence recorded against him.

passages.title: Maj Anil Kumar v Union of India (synthetic)
passages.text: Uncommunicated entries in the confidential reports cannot form the basis for refusing advancement; the selection board's decision was quashed.

passages.title: Sep Ramesh v Union of India (synthetic)
passages.text: A mishap on the journey between the unit and the place of residence during authorised absence is treated as connected with duty for the purpose of the award.

passages.title: Manual commentary on restrictions (synthetic)
passages.text: Members of the forces are barred from associating with any body of persons for collective bargaining and from participating in any concerted stoppage of work.

passages.title: Manual commentary on minor punishments (synthetic)
passages.text: The commanding officer may impose a pecuniary penalty not exceeding fourteen days' pay; anything beyond that requires a court-martial.

passages.title: Regimental estate note (synthetic)
passages.text: The football ground of the regimental centre was leased to the municipal corporation for the holidays; the lease money was credited to the regimental fund.

passages.title: Tribunal administration note (synthetic)
passages.text: The tribunal registry was shifted to a new building; cases filed late in the day will be listed for the following week, and parties may still look up the cause list online.

passages.title: Welfare note (synthetic)
passages.text: Wives of soldiers posted to operational areas may apply for separated family accommodation; the welfare section will support the application.

passages.title: Canteen note (synthetic)
passages.text: The commanding officer may order the closure of the unit canteen without any notice to the contractor if hygiene standards are not met in the army area.

passages.title: Training note (synthetic)
passages.text: A road accident involving a unit vehicle must be reported within twenty-four hours; the driver going on leave must hand over the vehicle log book.

passages.title: Pay office note (synthetic)
passages.text: Salary slips for the month are recovered from the pay office by the unit clerk; mistakes in the slips should be taken up with the pay office.

passages.title: The Synthetic Forces Act (synthetic)
passages.text: Period of limitation for trial. No trial by court-martial of any person shall be commenced after the expiration of three years from the date of the offence.

passages.title: The Synthetic Forces Act (synthetic)
passages.text: Absence without leave. Any person who absents himself without leave from his unit shall, on conviction by court-martial, be liable to imprisonment.

passages.title: The Synthetic Forces Rules (synthetic)
passages.text: Summary of evidence. The commanding officer shall have the summary of evidence recorded in the presence of the accused, who may cross-examine any witness.

passages.title: Entitlement commentary (synthetic)
passages.text: Disability pension is admissible where the disability is attributable to or aggravated by military service and assessed at twenty per cent or more.

passages.title: Manual commentary on custody (synthetic)
passages.text: A person subject to the Act who is charged with an offence may be taken into military custody under the orders of any superior officer.
